AthleteProfileUpdate.description:
Partial profile update.

Threshold fields (``hr_max``, ``resting_hr``, ``lthr``, ``threshold_pace``)
are written as a new ``athlete_thresholds`` step dated today, so editing a
threshold does not retroactively change how past activities are scored.

``lthr`` is accepted here because it is the reference for heart rate zones
and for hrTSS; without a write path the value could only ever come from a
seeded row, and the UI input for it silently discarded what the athlete
typed.
AthleteProfileUpdate.title: AthleteProfileUpdate

CoachContextReadinessResponse.description:
Readiness as the Today page consumes it.

Carries ``data_sufficient`` so the client can tell an assessed mid-range
score from the neutral 50 returned when nothing was measured — the two are
numerically identical but mean opposite things.
CoachContextReadinessResponse.title: CoachContextReadinessResponse

CoachRecentLoadResponse.description:
Recent load and whether CTL may be quoted.

``ctl_warming_up`` is true until enough history exists for the CTL EWMA to
have converged away from its zero seed. A consumer that states a CTL figure
must check it: early values describe the warm-up, not the athlete.
CoachRecentLoadResponse.title: CoachRecentLoadResponse

FlaggedActivity.description:
An activity that is ignored or in the trash.

Carries enough for a list row; the full activity payload is available from
the ordinary detail endpoint.
FlaggedActivity.title: FlaggedActivity

IgnoreResult.description: Outcome of ignoring or un-ignoring one activity.
IgnoreResult.title: IgnoreResult

LocalReadinessResponse.description:
Locally computed readiness.

``data_sufficient`` is the machine-readable answer to "was anything
measured". Without it a client can only infer that from the score — and a
score of 50 means both "assessed as middling" and "no data at all", which
are opposite messages. The UI previously string-matched the factor details
to tell them apart, which breaks the moment the wording changes.
LocalReadinessResponse.title: LocalReadinessResponse

PmcPointResponse.description:
One day of the PMC series.

``ctl_warming_up`` is true while the CTL value is still dominated by the
EWMA's zero seed rather than by the athlete's training. The value is still
returned so a chart can draw it, but anything that states a number to the
athlete must check this flag — a 42-day time constant needs roughly twice
that before the figure describes fitness rather than the warm-up.
PmcPointResponse.title: PmcPointResponse

recent_time_s.title: Recent Time S

RestoreResult.description: Outcome of undoing a soft delete.
RestoreResult.title: RestoreResult

ZoneSchemeResponse.description:
One selectable zone scheme, with whether its inputs are on file.

`available` is false when a required threshold is missing, and `missing`
names it, so the picker can explain why a scheme is disabled instead of
offering it and producing an empty zone table.
ZoneSchemeResponse.title: ZoneSchemeResponse

ZonesResponse.description:
Zone tables for the athlete's thresholds under their chosen scheme.

``hr_max``/``lthr``/``resting_hr`` are the resolved values the boundaries
were built from, so the client can show the inputs next to the output.
``hr_scheme`` names which rule produced the boundaries, and
``unavailable_requirements`` lists the fields a scheme still needs (empty
when ``hr_zones`` is populated) — without it the UI cannot tell "no zones
configured" from "this scheme needs a resting heart rate first".

``hr_max_estimated`` marks an age-predicted HRmax: Tanaka et al. report a
residual SD of 7-11 bpm, so an estimate must never be presented as a
measured value.
ZonesResponse.title: ZonesResponse
